title_en: Spencer Look and Jack VanDerhei: The Assumptions That Can Put Your Retirement at Risk
title_zh: Spencer Look 与 Jack VanDerHei：可能让你的退休陷入风险的种种假设
subtitle_zh: 两位 Morningstar 退休研究专家谈退休危机、社会保障改革与长期护理风险。
summary_zh: 本期 The Long View 由 Amy Arnott 与 Christine Benz 对话 Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies 的两位专家：退休研究副总监 Spencer Look 与退休研究总监 Jack VanDerHei（曾任 Employee Benefit Research Institute 研究总监）。中心成立约四年半，使命是用实证证据帮助政策制定者与计划发起方理解拟议立法、监管与计划设计之间的权衡。Look 介绍旗舰的美国退休结果模型：一个基于消费者财务调查（Survey of Consumer Finances）的家庭层面微观模拟，类似蒙特卡洛（Monte Carlo），纳入工资、储蓄、换工作时的提取、退休前提取、社会保障、支出、寿命与长期护理，输出退休与长寿的结果分布，而非止步于资产余额或替代率；其差异化在于动态刻画人们随年龄、收入、计划类型变化的行为。VanDerHei 补充他们有覆盖数千家 401(k)、数百万参与者的数据库，并谈到 Savers Match（修正 AGI 门槛较低）、机会缺口（coverage gap）、年金进入目标日期系列。两人共同结论是：退休规划界低估了长期护理的分量，且美国是否真有退休危机应更平衡看待。

turns.en: Hi and welcome to the Long View. I'm Amy Arnott, Portfolio Strategist for Morningstar. And I'm Christine Benz, Director of Personal Finance and Retirement Planning for Morningstar.
turns.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听 The Long View。我是 Amy Arnott，Morningstar 的组合策略师。我是 Christine Benz，Morningstar 的个人理财与退休规划总监。

turns.en: Today we're happy to welcome two guests from Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies. Spencer Luke is Associate Director of Retirement Studies for Morningstar and Jack Van Der Huy is Director of Retirement Studies for the Center and previously worked as the Research Director at the Employee Benefit Research Institute from 1996 through 2022.
turns.zh: 今天我们很高兴请到两位来自 Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies 的嘉宾。Spencer Look 是 Morningstar 的退休研究副总监，Jack VanDerHei 是该中心的退休研究总监，此前在 1996 到 2022 年间担任 Employee Benefit Research Institute 的研究总监。

turns.en: So Christine, Spencer and Jack both produce a lot of really helpful research on retirement outcomes, social security reform, and retirement policy.
turns.zh: 所以 Christine，Spencer 和 Jack 都产出了大量非常有用的研究，涵盖退休结果、社会保障改革和退休政策。

turns.en: So we'll get into all of those topics in our discussion. And one of the highlights was their more balanced take on whether there's really a retirement crisis in the U.S.
turns.zh: 所以我们会在讨论中涉及所有这些话题。其中一个亮点，就是他们对美国是否真的存在退休危机给出了更平衡的看法。

turns.en: We hear a lot of really dire warnings about that. And so I appreciated, you know, their take on where there's room for improvement as well as some data on maybe things aren't quite as bad as some people might have us believe.
turns.zh: 我们听到太多关于这个问题的严峻警告。所以我很欣赏，他们一方面指出哪里还有改进空间，另一方面用数据说明事情也许并不像有些人想让我们相信的那么糟。

turns.en: You won't be surprised to hear that I really like the discussion about long-term care. And Spencer and Jack have both concluded that the retirement planning community has underrated long-term care as a risk factor for people's retirement plans.
turns.zh: 你不会惊讶地听到，我特别喜欢关于长期护理的讨论。Spencer 和 Jack 都得出了同一个结论：退休规划界低估了长期护理作为人们退休计划风险因素的分量。

turns.en: So I like delving into that. All right. So let's get into the discussion. Jack and Spencer, welcome to the Longview. Happy to be here. Thank you so much for having us.
turns.zh: 所以我很想深入聊聊这个。好，那我们开始讨论吧。Jack 和 Spencer，欢迎收听 The Long View。很高兴来到这里，非常感谢邀请我们来。

turns.en: Well, thank you so much for joining us. Maybe you could start by giving us some quick background on the Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies.
turns.zh: 非常感谢你们加入我们。也许你可以先简单给我们介绍一下 Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies 的背景。

turns.en: How did the Center first get started? And what's the mission you're trying to accomplish? I'll jump in first if you don't mind, Spencer. The Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies actually started about four and a half years ago.
turns.zh: 这个中心最初是怎么创立的？你们想要实现的使命是什么？如果不介意的话，我先来说，Spencer。Morningstar Center for Retirement and Policy Studies 大约是在四年半前成立的。

turns.en: And what it is is a center that allows us to provide empirical evidence that lets policy makers, plan sponsors, and other stakeholders understand the trade-offs in terms of proposed legislation, proposed regulation, and different types of planned designs.
turns.zh: 它实际上是一个中心，让我们能够提供实证证据，让政策制定者、计划发起方和其他利益相关方理解拟议立法、拟议监管以及不同类型计划设计之间的权衡取舍。

turns.en: So instead of just coming up with a single headline number, we provide very, very detailed information. Spencer, I'm wondering if you can talk about one of the linchpins of the work that you do at the Center, the Morningstar model of U.S. retirement outcomes.
turns.zh: 所以我们不只是给出一个单一的头条数字，而是提供非常、非常详细的信息。Spencer，我想让你谈谈你们在中心所做工作的一个核心支柱——Morningstar 的美国退休结果模型。

turns.en: Can you talk about how it works and what makes it different from more traditional retirement analyses? Yes, I love this question. The model that you just referenced, that's like our flagship model for the Center, powers a lot of the work that we do.
turns.zh: 你能讲讲它是如何运作的，以及它与传统退休分析有何不同吗？是的，我很喜欢这个问题。你刚才提到的那个模型，是我们中心的旗舰模型，驱动着我们大量的工作。

turns.en: It is a household-level micro-simulation model, I think, you know, a Monte Carlo type of approach for the audience out there. We built this on top of a government survey, the Survey of Consumer Finances, which is a representative sample of the U.S. population.
turns.zh: 它是一个家庭层面的微观模拟模型，我想对听众来说可以理解为一种蒙特卡洛（Monte Carlo）方法。我们是在一项政府调查的基础上建立的，即消费者财务调查（Survey of Consumer Finances），它是美国人口的代表性样本。

turns.en: And then we model, you know, project as people go forward and work, do their career, kind of go into retirement. We are very granular with what we're doing, kind of echoing what Jack was saying with the mission and kind of goal of the Center.
turns.zh: 然后我们对人们向前推进进行建模、预测，他们工作、发展职业、进入退休。我们在细节上非常精细，某种程度上呼应了 Jack 刚才所说的中心的使命和目标。

turns.en: We incorporate people's wages, savings, job changes, you know, upon job change. Do they cash out their retirement plan? We reflect pre-retirement withdrawals, of course, moving into retirement.
turns.zh: 我们把人们的工资、储蓄、换工作纳入考量——换工作时他们是否会提取退休金计划里的钱。我们反映退休前提取，然后进入退休。

turns.en: We incorporate social security, spending models, longevity, long-term care. It's a very detailed model that goes through a lot of this really messiness in reality to, you know, produce a distribution of outcomes on retirement and comatoglacy.
turns.zh: 我们纳入社会保障、支出模型、寿命、长期护理。这是一个非常细致的模型，它会穿过现实中大量这种复杂混乱，从而产生一系列关于退休与长寿的结果分布。

turns.en: So the goal here is to analyze retirement and comatoglacy. We don't just stop at, you know, a wealth balance of a replacement rate. We use that approach to kind of look at how likely it is people can rent short of money in retirement.
turns.zh: 所以我们的目标是分析退休与长寿。我们不会止步于资产余额或替代率。我们用这种方法来看人们在退休中缺钱的可能性有多大。

turns.en: The really big differentiator for us is leaning into the behavior. So instead of assuming people follow a set schedule, you know, they always save 5%, 6%, just as a simple example, our frameworks are going to be dynamic.
turns.zh: 对我们来说，真正的重大差异化在于深入研究行为。所以我们的框架不是假设人们遵循固定的计划，比如总是储蓄 5%、6%——举个简单例子——我们的框架是动态的。

turns.en: They change and reflect as people have a new job, a new type of plan as they, you know, make more money, get older. Very clearly the empirical data shows that, you know, people's behaviors can change.
turns.zh: 它们会随着人们换工作、换计划类型、收入增加、年龄增长而变化并反映出来。很清楚，实证数据显示人们的行为是会改变的。

turns.en: And so we're reflecting that in our framework, and I think that's what really differentiates us with our modeling approach. So Jack, as Spencer alluded to, when you're building a model of retirement outcomes, you have to make a lot of assumptions, not only about markets, but also how people behave.
turns.zh: 所以我们在框架中反映了这一点，我认为这正是我们的建模方法真正与众不同的地方。Jack，正如 Spencer 提到的，当你构建一个退休结果模型时，你必须做很多假设，不仅是关于市场，还包括人们的行为。

turns.en: How do you, Spencer and the rest of your team, try to make sure that you're making reasonable assumptions around things like savings, retirement age, social security, etc., when you're trying to project retirement outcomes?
turns.zh: 你和 Spencer 以及你的团队，是如何确保在储蓄、退休年龄、社会保障等方面做出合理假设的，当你试图预测退休结果时？

turns.en: Well, we're very fortunate when it comes to working with 401k participants. One of the other simulation models we have, not the one that Spencer already talked about, is something that's built literally on millions of participants from thousands of different 401k plans.
turns.zh: 在研究 401(k) 参与者方面，我们非常幸运。我们拥有的另一个模拟模型——不是 Spencer 已经讲过的那个——是完全建立在来自数千家不同 401(k) 计划、数百万参与者之上的。

turns.en: So when it comes to the ability to actually observe how participants are going to react to various types of plan designs, as well as different types of investment options and different types of markets, we have probably the largest database for that available.
turns.zh: 所以在观察参与者会对各种计划设计、不同投资选项以及不同市场如何反应这方面，我们大概拥有可用的最大数据库。

turns.en: In terms of some of the other things that we model, we obviously are able to deal with the Morningstar Capital Market assumptions, as well as having a very, very rich database of different household behavior, whether it's during the accumulation stage or once they retire and something I'm sure Spencer's going to get into in more detail later, we're able to do a very, very detailed job looking at what kind of expenses individuals will have
turns.zh: 就我们建模的其他一些内容而言，我们当然能够处理 Morningstar 的资本市场假设，也拥有一个关于不同家庭行为的非常、非常丰富数据库，无论是在积累阶段还是退休后。我相信 Spencer 稍后会更详细地讲到这一点，我们能够非常细致地研究个人在退休时会面临什么样的支出

turns.en: in retirement, whether it's just basic consumption or whether it might be something like long-term care expenses. So let's talk about how people are doing.
turns.zh: ——无论是基本消费，还是长期护理支出这类东西。那么我们来谈谈人们的现状如何。

turns.en: One topic we've discussed with a number of guests over the years has been whether we have a retirement crisis in the U.S. Spencer, maybe you can talk about what the data actually tell us about that.
turns.zh: 多年来，我们与很多嘉宾讨论过一个话题，就是我们国家是否存在退休危机。Spencer，也许你可以谈谈数据实际上告诉了我们什么。

turns.en: Are Americans broadly underprepared for retirement or has the problem concentrated among certain groups? Yeah, thanks for the question, Christine.
turns.zh: 美国人是否普遍为退休准备不足，还是问题集中在某些群体？是的，谢谢你的问题，Christine。

turns.en: This is exactly what the Morningstar model of U.S. retirement outcomes can answer. We can answer this question. The discussion and discourse in the media on the crisis, I do think there's very clear perspectives.
turns.zh: 这正是 Morningstar 的美国退休结果模型能够回答的。我们能回答这个问题。关于危机的媒体报道和讨论，我确实认为有非常清晰的观点。

turns.en: We fall somewhere, I think, somewhere in the middle. We do think there are very clearly groups of people who, you know, our model is showing our underprepared, you know, higher rates of retirement income and adequacy.
turns.zh: 我们大概在中间位置。我们确实认为有非常明显的群体，我们的模型显示他们准备不足、退休收入充足率偏低。

turns.en: So there is a concentration. We do see it among people, you know, lower income workers, single women, black and Hispanic households, you know, groups, you know, such as these where there's a higher likelihood of running short of money.
turns.zh: 所以确实存在集中现象。我们在低收入工作者、单身女性、黑人和西班牙裔家庭等群体中看到，这些群体缺钱的可能性更高。

turns.en: Our overall status-cooled model shows that about 40 to 45 percent of the population is at risk of shortfalls. So, you know, a pretty sizable number.
turns.zh: 我们整体的现状基准模型显示，大约 40% 到 45% 的人口面临资金缺口的风险。所以，这是一个相当大的数字。

turns.en: That being said, what we did find in our research is that those who are consistently saving. So in our framework, we simulate people saving and participating in a plan, you know, regularly saving over time.
turns.zh: 话虽如此，我们在研究中确实发现，那些持续储蓄的人——在我们的框架中，我们模拟人们储蓄、参与计划、长期规律储蓄。

turns.en: The people who follow those paths tend to be in pretty good shape. So participating in a plan, saving, whatever that looks like for a worker, that can help quite a lot, I think, pretty intuitively, just the power of compounding and, you know, putting money aside.
turns.zh: 沿着这些路径走的人往往状况相当好。所以参与计划、储蓄，无论这对一名工作者意味着什么，那都能帮上大忙。我想这很直观，就是复利的力量和攒钱的好处。

turns.en: An interesting finding that I thought I'd mentioned here is that GenZ workers in our status-cooled analysis, they actually, they're looking a little bit better than some of the later, or I should say older age cohorts, where there was more disruption in terms of going from the DB to the DC system.
turns.zh: 我觉得这里值得提的一个有趣发现是，在我们的现状基准分析中，Z 世代（Gen Z）工作者实际上比一些年长群体看起来更好，那些年长群体从 DB（确定给付）转向 DC（确定缴付）体系时经历了更多动荡。

turns.en: So with GenZ workers, you know, as more DC plans and access is there, you know, we're actually seeing lower rates of retirement income and adequacy with GenZ.
turns.zh: 所以对 Z 世代工作者来说，随着更多 DC 计划和机会的出现，我们实际上看到 Z 世代退休收入缺口率更低。

turns.en: One last thing I wanted to highlight here is that long-term care costs has a really, really big impact on these numbers. And so, you know, just to kind of help people, as you kind of see this discourse in the media, long-term care is a really big impact.
turns.zh: 我最后想强调的一点是，长期护理成本对这些数字有非常大的影响。所以，就像你在媒体上看到的那些讨论一样，长期护理影响很大。

turns.en: If you ignore long-term care costs, we published a piece where we did this, and our estimates from that 40 to 45 percent number came down around 25 percent.
turns.zh: 如果你忽略长期护理成本——我们发表过一篇文章专门这样做了——我们估计的 40% 到 45% 这个数字就降到了大约 25%。

turns.en: So, you know, a really big impact. Do you think it makes sense to incorporate? There's a lot of uncertainty with long-term care. It's a very big issue that I think, you know, can't speak enough about it just to being prepared and educate people on that risk.
turns.zh: 所以，影响真的很大。你认为纳入……长期护理有很多不确定性，这是个非常大的问题，我认为怎么强调准备和教育都不为过。

turns.en: Yeah, we want to delve more into that, Spencer. But sticking with retirement crisis and retirement preparedness, you know, we hear a lot about today's economy being kind of a K-shape, where people who have market exposure have done really well, they're out there spending, and then lower economic strata are not participating in that.
turns.zh: 是的，Spencer，我们想更深入地谈这个。但先回到退休危机和退休准备度这个话题。我们经常听到今天的经济呈 K 型（K-shaped），有市场敞口的人做得很好、在外面消费，而较低的经济阶层没有从中受益。

turns.en: Do you see that in terms of retirement preparedness as well? Definitely. That's something that in our behavior estimates or our assumptions that Jack was kind of talking through, you do see that the likelihood of participating or saving into an IRA or participating in a retirement, you know, employer-sponsored plan for lower-income workers.
turns.zh: 在退休准备度方面你也看到这种情况吗？当然。那正是我们在行为估计或假设中——Jack 之前讲过的——你会看到低收入工作者参与或向 IRA 储蓄、或参与雇主退休计划的可能性。

turns.en: As an example, it tends to be less than higher-income, middle-income workers. And so, that dynamic definitely is at play. It's something that does help inform our estimates of lower-income workers, you know, there's a pretty good chance they could run short of money.
turns.zh: 举个例子，它往往低于中高收入工作者。所以这种动态确实在起作用。它确实帮助我们估计低收入工作者很有可能会缺钱。

turns.en: That's also what I think is part of the motivation behind some of the policies that we've seen that have come across our desk that are trying to get universal market participation or universal in, you know, U.S. workers participating in the market.
turns.zh: 我认为这也是我们经手的一些政策背后的部分动机，那些试图实现普遍市场参与、让所有美国工作者都参与市场的政策。

turns.en: That's exactly the thought behind that, where folks who traditionally may not have access to an advisor, may not be saving, may not really prioritize that, can kind of start and then start building equity and try to, you know, kind of help out and out front.
turns.zh: 那正是其背后的想法，让那些传统上可能接触不到顾问、可能没在储蓄、可能不太重视这一点的人，可以起步、开始积累财富，从而提前获得帮助。

turns.en: So it is something that we see and it's something that, you know, there's policy initiatives that are going to try to address that and so we'll see how that plays out.
turns.zh: 所以这是我们看到的现象，也有一些政策倡议会试图解决这个问题，我们拭目以待它会如何发展。

turns.en: So when you're evaluating those types of policy initiatives, what type of criteria do you think policymakers and researchers should use to determine whether a proposal actually improves retirement outcomes and long-term retirement security?
turns.zh: 当你在评估这类政策倡议时，你认为政策制定者和研究者应该用什么标准来判断一项提案是否真的能改善退休结果和长期退休安全？

turns.en: Can I start by bifurcating between social security reform, which I'm sure is going to be on the top of most people's list of things they want to talk about soon and just general retirement plan proposals.
turns.zh: 我可以先把社会保障改革和一般的退休计划提案分开来谈，社会保障改革我相信很快就会排在很多人想讨论的事情清单首位。

turns.en: So if it's a letter, if we're not talking about social security reform, I think the thing that people have to keep in mind when a proposal comes up is that access has to come first.
turns.zh: 所以如果是一份法案，如果我们不谈社会保障改革，我认为当一项提案出现时，人们必须记住的是，机会（access）必须排在第一位。

turns.en: After that, you can talk about participation, contribution rates, escalation, employer contributions, leakages, job change, retirement age. That all matters, but if they're not in a plan, basically they don't have the ability to participate in this.
turns.zh: 在那之后，你才能谈参与率、缴存比例、自动递增、雇主缴付、渗漏、换工作、退休年龄。这些都重要，但如果他们根本不在计划里，基本上他们就没有参与的能力。

turns.en: The thing that I think you really have to keep in mind is that behavior on the part of the participant is going to matter basically as much as the markets.
turns.zh: 我认为你真正必须记住的一点是，参与者的行为基本上和市场同样重要。

turns.en: You can have a model that very carefully looks at different returns but assumes a way actual participant behavior and that is basically going to produce, in essence, a really precise answer to the wrong question.
turns.zh: 你可以有一个非常仔细地审视不同回报的模型，却假设了一种不真实的参与者行为，那基本上会给出对一个错误问题的极其精确的答案。
